sources.locator: Contents at PDF p. 5 lists Section 2.9 "Summations over divisors"; read the Section 2.9 development and exercises on printed pp. 45-49 / PDF pp. 62-66, especially the arithmetic-function and Dirichlet-product introduction together with Exercises 2.49-2.54.

Exercise 2.52 on the squarefree-weighted divisor sum
contents.reason: This exercise packages a separate squarefree divisor identity that the NT-9 design does not consume. It belongs with later average-order and Euler-product calculations, not with the present finite convolution core.

contents.name: Exercise 2.53 on squarefree detection by a divisor sum
contents.reason: The page already uses the published Mobius supplier items and does not need a second squarefree-detection criterion. Carrying this exercise here would add an attractive but nonessential side identity.

contents.name: Subsection 23.4.1 The monoid of arithmetic functions
Corollary 23.4.4
contents.reason: The current page explicitly reuses the already-published Mobius supplier items from incidence-algebras-and-mobius-inversion. Rebuilding the special case mu = u^{-1} here would duplicate earlier published content under a new local carrier.

contents.name: Remark 23.4.7
contents.reason: The remark points ahead to valuations, derivations, and broader ring-theoretic structure of arithmetic functions. NT-9 deliberately stops before those later Dirichlet-series and Euler-product developments.

sources.title: Tom Sanders, Topics in Analytic Number Theory
sources.locator: Read Section 1 "Arithmetic functions", PDF pp. 1-5, lines 2-394, including the definition of Lambda, Proposition 1.1, Theorem 1.2, Propositions 1.3-1.5, the displayed identity 1 * Lambda = log, and the definition of M(n).

contents.name: the definition of the von Mangoldt function Lambda
Proposition 1.3
contents.reason: This harmonic-sum asymptotic is not part of the finite convolution package itself. The next number-theory page is the one that turns divisor identities into average-order estimates and therefore owns this quantitative logarithm lemma.

contents.name: Proposition 1.4
contents.reason: Dirichlet's hyperbola estimate for the summatory divisor function is exactly next-page material. NT-9 builds tau and the convolution algebra first, then NT-10 uses them for average-order and error-term statements.

contents.name: the definition M(n) = sum_{x <= n} mu(x)
Proposition 1.5
contents.reason: This proposition is the first quantitative bridge from summatory Mobius cancellation to the prime number theorem. It belongs to the later page where M(x), Abel summation, and average-order arguments become load-bearing rather than merely definitional.
